arxiv-2107-04436.title: Large Scale Measurement on the Adoption of Encrypted DNS 418
arxiv-2107-04436.creator: Sebastián García, Karel Hynek, Dmtrii Vekshin, Tomáš Čejka, Armin Wasicek
arxiv-2107-04436.description: Abstract . Several encryption proposals for DNS have been presented since 2016, but their adoption was not comprehensively studied yet. This research measured the current adoption of DoH (DNS over HTTPS), DoT (DNS over TLS), and DoQ (DNS over QUIC) for five months at the beginning of 2021 by three different organizations with global coverage.

arxiv-2107-12127.title: Operator spectrum of nonrelativistic CFTs at large charge
arxiv-2107-12127.creator: Vito Pellizzani
arxiv-2107-12127.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Vito Pellizzani. We extend and clarify the large-charge expansion of the conformal dimension Δ Q \Delta_{Q} of the lowest operator of charge Q Q in nonrelativistic conformal field theories using the state-operator correspondence. The latter requires coupling the theory to an external harmonic trap that confines the particles to a spherical cloud, at the edge of which the effective theory breaks down and leads to divergences.

arxiv-2208-07468.title: Encoding Integers and Rationals on Neuromorphic Computers using Virtual Neuron
arxiv-2208-07468.creator: Prasanna Date, Catherine Schuman, Shruti Kulkarni, Thomas Potok, Aaron Young, Jeffrey Vetter
arxiv-2208-07468.description: Abstract Neuromorphic computers perform computations by emulating the human brain, and use extremely low power. They are expected to be indispensable for energy-efficient computing in the future. While they are primarily used in spiking neural network-based machine learning applications, neuromorphic computers are known to be Turing-complete, and thus, capable of general-purpose computation.

arxiv-2403-05306.title: A Collaborative Robot-Assisted Manufacturing Assembly Process
arxiv-2403-05306.creator: Miguel Neves 1, Laura Duarte 1, Pedro Neto 1
arxiv-2403-05306.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Miguel Neves 1, Laura Duarte 1, Pedro Neto 1. An effective human-robot collaborative process results in the reduction of the operator’s workload, promoting a more efficient, productive, safer and less error-prone working environment. However, the implementation of collaborative robots in industry is still challenging. In this work, we compare manual and robot-assisted assembly processes to evaluate the effectiveness of collaborative robots while featuring different modes of operation (coexistence, cooperation and collaboration).

arxiv-2411-01790.title: Thinking Forward and Backward: Effective Backward Planning with Large Language Models
arxiv-2411-01790.creator: Allen Z. Ren, Brian Ichter, Anirudha Majumdar
arxiv-2411-01790.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have exhibited remarkable reasoning and planning capabilities. Most prior work in this area has used LLMs to reason through steps from an initial to a goal state or criterion, thereby effectively reasoning in a forward direction.

arxiv-2412-06842.title: Partition of Unity Physics-Informed Neural Networks (POU-PINNs): An Unsupervised Framework for Physics-Informed Domain Decomposition and Mixtures of Experts
arxiv-2412-06842.creator: Arturo Rodriguez, Ashesh Chattopadhyay, Piyush Kumar, Luis F. Rodriguez, Vinod Kumar
arxiv-2412-06842.description: Abstract Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) commonly address ill-posed inverse problems by uncovering unknown physics. This study presents a novel unsupervised learning framework that identifies spatial subdomains with specific governing physics. It uses the partition of unity networks (POUs) to divide the space into subdomains, assigning unique nonlinear model parameters to each, which are integrated into the physics model.

arxiv-2501-18710.title: Forcing Axioms for Proper Posets Preserving a Topological Property: Consistency Results
arxiv-2501-18710.creator: Thomas Gilton
arxiv-2501-18710.description: Abstract . Forcing axioms are generalizations of Baire category principles that allow one to intersect more dense open sets and to do so in a wider variety of circumstances. In this paper we introduce two new forcing axioms related to posets which preserve topological properties of various spaces, specifically the properties of Lindelöf and countably tight.

arxiv-2601-00752.title: Three results on twisted G − G- codes and skew twisted G − G- codes
arxiv-2601-00752.creator: Alvaro Otero Sanchez, aos073@ual.es
arxiv-2601-00752.description: Abstract In this paper, we solve an open question posed in the original paper on twisted skew group codes concerning the conditions under which a twisted skew group code is checkable. We also prove that all ideals of dimension three over a twisted group algebra are abelian group codes, thereby generalizing a previous result for group algebras.

Rojas, Diyar Saeed, Bastian Schmack, Gregor Warnecke, Daniel Zimpfer, Herko Grubitzsch, Volkmar Falk, Evgenij Pot
pmc-10608612.description: Mechanical circulatory support has proven effective in managing postcardiotomy cardiogenic shock by stabilizing patients’ hemodynamics and ensuring adequate organ perfusion. Among the available device modalities, the combination of extracorporeal life support and a microaxial flow pump for left ventricular unloading has emerged as a valuable tool in the surgical armamentarium.

pmc-11558125.title: Titania‐Based Coral‐Structured Solar Absorber Coating with Improved Scalability and Durability at High Temperature
pmc-11558125.creator: Yifan Guo, Kaoru Tsuda, Milad Mohsenzadeh, Sahar Hosseini, Yasushi Murakami, Joe Coventry, Juan F Torres
pmc-11558125.description: Solar energy harvesting and storage are essential in the future mix of renewable energy technologies. Hierarchical coral‐structured coatings have been shown to yield high solar absorptance in concentrating solar thermal (CST) systems. However, interfacial delamination and scalability challenges owing to material complexity pose significant hurdles for the widespread industrial adoption of these hierarchical CST coatings.

pmc-11635709.title: Impact of drying techniques on volatile aroma profiles and formation mechanisms of black soybean thua nao
pmc-11635709.creator: Pakavit Mathatheeranan, Ting-Jang Lu, Thanakorn Wongprasert, Yi-Ci Jhu, Hsin-Jo Chang, Wei-Yuan Wu, Mingchih Fang, Kitipong Assatarakul, Inthawoot Suppavorasatit
pmc-11635709.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Thua nao, a traditional Thai fermented soybean, offers a unique aroma and nutritional value. However, fresh thua nao cannot be stored for long periods due to its high in water activity (aw). This study examined the effects of various drying methods, including natural sun drying and machine drying methods, namely hot air, microwave vacuum (MIC), and vacuum drying on the qualities of dried black soybean thua nao.

pmc-13029403.title: Trends in Arthrospira sp. (Spirulina) Applications: A 15-Year Bibliometric Analysis and Systematic Review
pmc-13029403.creator: Hoda Hosseini, Touria Bounnit, Imen Saadaoui
pmc-13029403.description: Due to their exceptional nutritional benefits, microalgae and cyanobacteria are recognized as sustainable food sources and key contributors to the circular bioeconomy. Arthrospira sp. has garnered significant attention as one of the most promising cyanobacteria for a wide range of applications. The purpose of this study is to systematically analyze and synthesize global research trends in Arthrospira sp. applications.

pmc-13183743.title: Finesse in Forehead Lifting—Asymmetric Ligament Release for Asymmetric Brow Ptosis
pmc-13183743.creator: Henry Bair, Tiffany S Cheng, Sathyadeepak Ramesh
pmc-13183743.description: BackgroundAsymmetric brow ptosis presents a unique surgical challenge. It has been traditionally managed with full deep-plane release of the forehead retaining ligaments, which often leads to overcorrection or persistent asymmetry. This case series evaluates an approach using titrated asymmetric ligament release and selective fixation to address brow asymmetry while minimizing complications.

pmc-13336154.title: Implementing community case management of malaria: Stakeholder insights on advancing equitable access in Kilifi County
pmc-13336154.creator: Evelyn Waweru, Moses Chapa Kiti, Grace Masha, Benjamin Tsofa, Gabriele Paone, George Dzombo, Gabriele Cerini, Maria Vittoria De Vita, Gianfranco Morino, Federico Gobbi, Paolo Leoncini, Edward Chimwaga Mwamuye, Simon Chengo Masha, Louisa Messenger, Louisa Messenger, Louisa Messenger
pmc-13336154.description: Malaria detection in Kilifi, County, primarily relies on intermittent active surveillance at healthcare facilities. To strengthen control of uncomplicated malaria, community health promoters (CHPs) were engaged in community health education, case detection, and treatment. This study examines lessons from integrating CHPs in community case management of malaria (CCMm).

pmc-13556576.title: 613. The analysis of the impact of non-steroidal drug and the TRP compound on the immune profile of microglia: study in an Alzheimer’s disease model
pmc-13556576.creator: E Trojan, K Kamińska, M Leśkiewicz, M Regulska, B Grygier, J Frydrych, A Basta-Kaim
pmc-13556576.description: BackgroundNeuroinflammation is a hallmark of central nervous system (CNS) disorders and plays a critical role in the progression of neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease. Microglia, the resident immune cells of the CNS, act as key regulators of inflammatory responses and are rapidly activated in response to pathological stimuli such as amyloid-β accumulation, neuronal injury, and synaptic dysfunction.
